messages:
marta: quick cost-quality snapshot for sable9b int6 vs int8 — want ops + product recs before handing to GTN.

marta: ran slice-based evals on our chat QA set + a 2k-turn contextual search workload. microbench + eval in the sandbox.

marta: TL;DR: int6 = ~36% cost reduction, median latency +8ms, P95 +22ms, EM drop 0.9pp on prod-like blind set. tradeoffs look acceptable for non-precision-critical flows. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sam: can you paste the numbers? short table would help.

marta: sure — pasted from the run:
```
Model        | Cost/token | median_lat(ms) | p95_lat(ms) | EM(qa) |
sable9b-int8 | 1.00x      | 87             | 210         | 74.8%  |
sable9b-int6 | 0.64x      | 95             | 232         | 73.9%  |
Delta        | -36%       | +8ms           | +22ms       | -0.9pp |
```

marta: breakdown by slice: hallucination-heavy prompts saw bigger EM drop (~1.8pp). short factual Qs almost identical.

leo: important: latency p95 increase is small but visible. for chat product that holds websocket sessions, 22ms p95 is fine. for low-latency search rerank maybe not.

alyssa: product note — GTN wants <1pp regression overall and strong per-slice guardrails. 0.9pp borderline but ok if we gate high-risk slices to int8.

sam: ops note: recommend canary 5-10% traffic + continuous eval on the live eval set, auto rollback if slice EM drop >1.2pp or p95 increase >40ms. agree?

marta: +1. propose routing policy in the console with a tag-based fallback. pseudo-config:
```
routes:
  - name: sable9b-primary
    model: sable9b-int6
    fallback: sable9b-int8
    canary: 0.1
    slices:
      - name: "hallucination_sensitive"
        policy: force_fallback
```

leo: small nit: add kv-cache-preserve=true for canary to reduce cache-warmup noise in perf metrics.

alyssa: product OK with 10% canary if we enforce slice gating and upload the slice-level diff report to GTN dashboard daily.

canary-bot: deploy started for canary (10%) — tracking ID cb-349876-sable9b — will post hourly eval snapshots.

sam: will add CI monitors: eval-run every 15m, alert to #incidents if conditional thresholds breached.

marta: next steps: (1) start 10% canary now, (2) spawn gated route for hallucination_sensitive -> int8, (3) daily sign-off with GTN after 48h if no regressions. Ill draft the handoff note for GTN.

alyssa: sounds good. please include cost projections for 30/70 int6/int8 steady-state vs 100% int8 for finance.

marta: will do — quick projection: steady 30/70 = ~20% cost savings vs 100% int8, with near-zero quality loss on product slices.

leo: 👍 from infra. keep an eye on memory OOMs after quant rollout.

sam: tagging @oncall for visibility. :bell:

marta: thanks all — I'll post the handoff doc shortly and link the canary metrics.
